arxiv-2112-09293.title: A Comparative Study of Detecting Anomalies in Time Series Data Using LSTM and TCN Models
arxiv-2112-09293.creator: Saroj Gopali 1 , Faranak Abri 1 , Sima Siami-Namini 2 , and Akbar Siami Namin 1 1 Department of Computer Science, 2 School of Planning and Public Policy 1 Texas Tech University, 2 Rutgers University { saroj.gopali | | faranak.abri | | akbar.namin } @ttu.edu and sima.siaminamini@rutgers.edu
arxiv-2112-09293.description: Abstract There exist several data-driven approaches that enable us model time series data including traditional regression-based modeling approaches (i.e., ARIMA). Recently, deep learning techniques have been introduced and explored in the context of time series analysis and prediction. A major research question to ask is the performance of these many variations of deep learning techniques in predicting time series data.

arxiv-2201-05474.creator: Lian Wu, Runlian Xia, Dejian Zhou
arxiv-2201-05474.description: Abstract . In this paper, we establish noncommutative Burkholder inequalities with asymmetric diagonals in symmetric operator spaces. Our proof mainly relies on a noncommutative good- λ \lambda approach and a new complex interpolation result on asymmetric vector valued spaces. We include as well the asymmetric versions of noncommutative Johnson-Schechtman inequalities. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary: 46L53, 60G42; Secondary: 46L52 1.

arxiv-2203-12627.title: First Light And Reionisation Epoch Simulations (FLARES) IV: The size evolution of galaxies at z ≥ 5 z\geq 5 2022 First Light And Reionisation Epoch Simulations (FLARES) IV: The size evolution of galaxies at z ≥ 5 z\geq 5 – 5
arxiv-2203-12627.creator: William J. Roper, Christopher C. Lovell, Aswin P. Vijayan, Madeline A. Marshall, Dimitrios Irodotou, Jussi K. Kuusisto, Peter A. Thomas, Stephen M. Wilkins
arxiv-2203-12627.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by William J. Roper, Christopher C. Lovell, Aswin P. Vijayan, Madeline A. Marshall, Dimitrios Irodotou, Jussi K. Kuusisto, Peter A. Thomas, Stephen M. Wilkins. We present the intrinsic and observed sizes of galaxies at z ≥ 5 z\geq 5 in the First Light And Reionisation Epoch Simulations (FLARES). We employ the large effective volume of FLARES to produce a sizeable sample of high redshift galaxies with intrinsic and observed luminosities and half light radii in a range of rest frame UV and visual photometric bands.

arxiv-2208-14385.title: Application of Convolutional Neural Networks with Quasi-Reversibility Method Results for Option Forecasting
arxiv-2208-14385.creator: Zheng Cao 1, Wenyu Du 2, Kirill V. Golubnichiy 3
arxiv-2208-14385.description: Abstract This paper presents a novel way to apply mathematical finance and machine learning (ML) to forecast stock options prices. Following the previous results, we create and evaluate new empirical mathematical models for the Black-Scholes equation to analyze data for 92,846 companies.

arxiv-2305-16884.title: Solving the cohomological equation for locally hamiltonian flows, part I - local obstructions
arxiv-2305-16884.creator: Krzysztof Frączek, Minsung Kim
arxiv-2305-16884.description: Abstract . We study the cohomological equation X ​ u = f Xu=f for smooth locally Hamiltonian flows on compact surfaces. The main novelty of the proposed approach is that it is used to study the regularity of the solution u u when the flow has saddle loops, which has not been systematically studied before.

arxiv-2307-09950.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Junjielong Xu, Ruichun Yang, Yintong Huo, Chengyu Zhang, Pinjia He. Log parsing, which involves log template extraction from semi-structured logs to produce structured logs, is the first and the most critical step in automated log analysis. However, current log parsers suffer from limited effectiveness for two reasons. First , traditional data-driven log parsers solely rely on heuristics or handcrafted features designed by domain experts, which may not consistently perform well on logs from diverse systems.

arxiv-2312-05057.title: Parametrically enhancing sensor sensitivity at an exceptional point
arxiv-2312-05057.creator: P. Djorwé, M. Asjad, Y. Pennec, D. Dutykh, B. Djafari-Rouhani
arxiv-2312-05057.description: Abstract We propose a scheme to enhance the sensitivity of Non-Hermitian optomechanical mass-sensors. The benchmark system consists of two coupled optomechanical systems where the mechanical resonators are mechanically coupled. The optical cavities are driven either by a blue or red detuned laser to produce gain and loss, respectively.

arxiv-2402-10510.title: Human Goal Recognition as Bayesian Inference: Investigating the Impact of Actions, Timing, and Goal Solvability Conference: Proc. of the 23rd International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems (AAMAS 2024); May 6 – 10, 2024; Auckland, New Zealand 1004
arxiv-2402-10510.creator: Chenyuan Zhang, Charles Kemp, Nir Lipovetzky
arxiv-2402-10510.description: Abstract . Goal recognition is a fundamental cognitive process that enables individuals to infer intentions based on available cues. Current goal recognition algorithms often take only observed actions as input, but here we use a Bayesian framework to explore the role of actions, timing, and goal solvability in goal recognition.

arxiv-2404-06612.title: Small fluctuations for time-dependent spherical random fields Thanks: 1 1 footnotemark: 1 † {\dagger} Research was supported in part by an AMS-Simons Travel Grant Thanks: 2 2 footnotemark: 2 ⋆ \star Research was supported in part by “INdAM - GNAMPA Project”, codice CUP E53C23001670001.
arxiv-2404-06612.creator: Marco Carfagnini †, Anna Paola Todino ⋆
arxiv-2404-06612.description: Abstract . We consider time-dependent space isotropic and time stationary spherical Gaussian random fields. We establish Chung’s law of the iterated logarithm and solve the small probabilities problem. Our results depend on the high-frequency behaviour of the angular power spectrum: the speed of decay of the small ball probability is faster as either the memory parameter or the space-parameter decreases.

arxiv-2407-13226.title: Towards a complete picture of the Sco-Cen outflow
arxiv-2407-13226.creator: M. Piecka, S. Hutschenreuter, J. Alves
arxiv-2407-13226.description: Abstract Previous studies have shown strong evidence that the Sun is crossing an outflow originating from the Sco-Cen OB association. Understanding this outflow’s origin and structure illuminates how massive star formation shapes the interstellar medium (ISM) and helps predict future Galactic conditions affecting our Solar System.

arxiv-2505-12154.title: Learning to Highlight Audio by Watching Movies
arxiv-2505-12154.creator: Chao Huang, Ruohan Gao, J. M. F. Tsang, Jan Kurcius, Cagdas Bilen, Chenliang Xu, Anurag Kumar, Sanjeel Parekh
arxiv-2505-12154.description: Abstract Recent years have seen a significant increase in video content creation and consumption. Crafting engaging content requires the careful curation of both visual and audio elements. While visual cue curation, through techniques like optimal viewpoint selection or post-editing, has been central to media production, its natural counterpart, audio, has not undergone equivalent advancements.

pmc-10504266.title: Selective effects of estradiol on human corneal endothelial cells
pmc-10504266.creator: Seoyoung Han, Christian Mueller, Caitlin Wuebbolt, Sean Kilcullen, Varinda Nayyar, Brayan Calle Gonzalez, Ali Mahdavi Fard, Jamie C. Floss, Michael J. Morales, Sangita P. Patel
pmc-10504266.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). In Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy (FECD), mitochondrial and oxidative stresses in corneal endothelial cells (HCEnCs) contribute to cell demise and disease progression. FECD is more common in women than men, but the basis for this observation is poorly understood. To understand the sex disparity in FECD prevalence, we studied the effects of the sex hormone 17-β estradiol (E2) on growth, oxidative stress, and metabolism in primary cultures of HCEnCs grown under physiologic ([O2]2.5) and hyperoxic ([O2]A) conditions.

pmc-11554547.title: Effect of Processed Coffee Husk on Feed Intake, Nutrient Digestibility, Body Weight Changes and Economic Feasibility of Bonga Sheep Fed on Natural Pasture Hay as a Basal Diet
pmc-11554547.creator: Lidya Marew, Fentahun Meheret, Bimrew Asmare
pmc-11554547.description: BackgroundEthiopia is one of the world's coffee producers, generating about 192,000 metric tonnes of coffee husks annually as by‐products. The material can be used for ruminant diets to improve the nutrient utilisation of animals. However, coffee husk has toxic compounds, which can be minimised through different processing methods.

pmc-11675572.title: Identification of ncRNA Biomarkers in Non–Small Cell Lung Cancer to Address Racial Disparities
pmc-11675572.creator: Lu Gao, Pushpa Dhilipkannah, Feng Jiang
pmc-11675572.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Lung cancer significantly impacts mortality, with African Americans (AA) showing higher rates than White Americans (WA). ncRNAs play a crucial role in lung tumorigenesis. To identify ncRNA biomarkers associated with racial disparities in lung cancer, we used droplet digital PCR to examine 93 lung cancer–associated ncRNAs in plasma and sputum samples from participants of AA and WA backgrounds, including 118 patients and 92 cancer-free smokers.

pmc-12468359.title: Clinical and Molecular Profiling of Colorectal Cancer: A Comprehensive Cohort Study of BRAF-Mutated Cases from a Tertiary Centre
pmc-12468359.creator: Julia Freckelton, Justin Mencel, Iris Levink, Sheela Rao, Charlotte Fribbens, Paula Proszek, Damian Brooks, Xin Liu, David Cunningham, Ian Chau, Naureen Starling
pmc-12468359.description: Simple SummaryColorectal cancer is a common disease, and a specific genetic change called a BRAF mutation is often used by doctors to guide treatment decisions. However, not all BRAF mutations are the same, and patients with these mutations can experience very different outcomes.

pmc-12565298.title: Pareto-Efficient Utilization of Coated Vermiculite Aggregate in High-Strength Lightweight Mortar with Mohr–Coulomb Parameter Analysis
pmc-12565298.creator: Zeynep Algin, Muhammed Şerif Yoluk, Halil Murat Algin, Antonio Caggiano
pmc-12565298.description: A multilayered coating process, based on cement and silica fume, was applied to the surface of expanded vermiculite aggregate (EVA) using a cold bonding method. This investigation represents the first systematic study of this multilayered coating method, with the objective of evaluating the effectiveness of coating thickness in the production of high-performance lightweight mortar.

pmc-12595217.title: Nanoparticle-based approaches for wound healing: a comprehensive review of nanomaterials enhancing tissue regeneration
pmc-12595217.creator: Pritam Paul, Sushruta S Hakkimane
pmc-12595217.description: Wound healing is a complex biological process involving multiple stages that require interactions between several cells, growth factors, and cytokines. The lack of a suitable environment, along with microbial infection, impairs the normal wound-healing process. Burns, trauma, diabetic injuries, and chronic ulcers are the most prevalent types of wounds on the skin.

pmc-13213589.title: Dementia diagnostic deserts: workforce and geographic inequities in the diagnostic pathway for cognitive impairment
pmc-13213589.creator: Zhijing Xu, Ying Xue, Yaguang Zheng, Bei Wu
pmc-13213589.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). As disease-modifying therapies for Alzheimer's disease become available, ensuring equitable access to timely and accurate diagnosis of cognitive impairment is critical. This article conceptualizes “dementia diagnostic deserts,” defined as geographic areas where rurality, primary care professional shortages, and high social deprivation converge to exacerbate access to the diagnostic continuum, from initial screening and comprehensive evaluation to the appropriate referral for specialist-based diagnostic confirmation.
